chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died and left behind a slave, and one of his children testified that their father had freed him, he said: 'His testimony is accepted, and he is not held financially responsible, and the slave must work to compensate the share that belonged to the other heirs.'

key_terms.أَعْتَقَهُ: He freed him (emancipation of a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one heir testifies that their father freed a slave?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling to clarify the evidentiary weight of a single heir's testimony regarding the emancipation of a shared slave, ensuring that the testifying child is not financially penalized for their claim. The slave remains bound to compensate the other heirs for their respective shares of the slave's value, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of balancing individual rights with collective inheritance equity. This highlights the practical application of 'shahada' (testimony) in transactional matters within the family unit.
